rationale: The assistant correctly decoded 'FD 9409' as a 2014 production code rather than a model or error code, asked for the E-Nr, and ordered sensible checks (listen to pump, turn impeller, hoses, display code) before buying anything; safety steps (unplug, drain via emergency hose, water off) were included. After the customer reported hum + E18 + stiff gritty impeller it declared 'Yes, it's the drain pump' with no hedging, although the ground truth leaves a sump/tub-to-pump hose blockage genuinely open and the claim that a blockage 'would usually free up once the filter is cleaned' is shaky - it only told him to check that hose once the pump was already out. It avoided naming a specific part number without the E-Nr and gave reasonable ways to identify the pump, but never suggested an engineer as an option for a customer who can't read the model label and may not want to go beyond the filter.
